note: DXPR Builder is a commercial front-end drag-and-drop page builder. It is enabled on a field by setting that field's view-display formatter to dxpr_builder_text (field types text/text_long/text_with_summary). The live editor needs a valid JWT/API key + billable-user license (DxprBuilderLicenseService), which this base site does NOT have, so cases are grounded in config/permissions/entities, not the live editor. Global settings live in config object dxpr_builder.settings; config entity types are dxpr_builder_profile (per-role allow-lists; config prefix dxpr_builder.dxpr_builder_profile.<id>), dxpr_builder_page_template, dxpr_builder_user_template. Permissions: 'edit with dxpr builder', 'administer dxpr builder configuration', 'administer dxpr_builder_profile'. Medium introspection reads back a known profile's roles; hard execution switches a field's view-display formatter to dxpr_builder_text, verified against the live entity_view_display.

evals.prompt: How do I make an existing body/text field on a Drupal content type editable with DXPR Builder's drag-and-drop editor? Name the field formatter involved.
evals.expected_output: DXPR Builder is a field formatter (id dxpr_builder_text) for text/text_long/text_with_summary fields. On the content type's Manage display, set the text field's format to 'DXPR Builder' (or set core.entity_view_display.<entity>.<bundle>.<mode> component type to dxpr_builder_text). Users need the 'edit with dxpr builder' permission to edit in place.

evals.prompt: What permissions does DXPR Builder provide and what does each one gate?
evals.expected_output: Three: 'edit with dxpr builder' (use the front-end builder to edit content; relevant to billable-user counting), 'administer dxpr builder configuration' (DXPR Studio admin: settings, AI settings, license/content pages), and 'administer dxpr_builder_profile' (create/edit the per-role dxpr_builder_profile entities). Page/user template routes additionally require core 'administer site configuration'.

evals.prompt: In DXPR Builder, how do I restrict which elements and templates a particular role can use, and what config entity types does the module provide?
evals.expected_output: Create a DXPR Builder Profile (dxpr_builder_profile config entity) that binds one or more roles to allow-lists of elements, blocks, views, page_templates and user_templates (with all_* booleans to allow everything of a kind). The module provides three config entity types: dxpr_builder_profile, dxpr_builder_page_template, and dxpr_builder_user_template. Managed under DXPR Studio (/admin/dxpr_studio/dxpr_builder).

evals.prompt: Where does DXPR Builder store its license/API (JWT) key, and what is the recommended, more secure option? Which config object holds the general settings?
evals.expected_output: General settings live in the dxpr_builder.settings config object. The JWT can be stored directly in config (json_web_token) or, preferably, in a Key entity by setting api_key_storage to 'key' and key_provider to a Key id (requires the key module). Access to the editor is gated by the billable-user license check.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a DXPR Builder profile with the machine id 'dxprb_known'. Inspect the live configuration and state which user role(s) that profile applies to.
evals.expected_output: The dxpr_builder_profile dxprb_known targets the 'authenticated' role (dxpr_builder.dxpr_builder_profile.dxprb_known -> roles: [authenticated]).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Article content type has a long-text field field_dxprb_body. Configure the default view display so this field is rendered/edited with DXPR Builder instead of the plain text formatter. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In core.entity_view_display.node.article.default the field_dxprb_body component has type 'dxpr_builder_text' (e.g. $vd->setComponent('field_dxprb_body', ['type'=>'dxpr_builder_text',...])->save();).

evals.prompt: I want to edit the 'DXPRB Body' field on my Article pages with the DXPR drag-and-drop builder instead of a plain text box. Please switch it over on my site.
evals.expected_output: Same verified end state as the expert variant: field_dxprb_body's component in the Article default view display uses the dxpr_builder_text formatter.
